headline: High: AutoGPT can write and execute shell commands while social-auto-upload can upload account-linked media, creating dangerous default-path conflicts and possible prompt/data leakage through shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while social-auto-upload uses filesystem inputs like videos and images. If AutoGPT places attacker-controlled text into shared files, social-auto-upload may ingest it as content or metadata. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF AutoGPT writes instruction-like content into files that social-auto-upload later reads
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Review uploaded captions and metadata before posting
Add a manual approval step for any file consumed by social-auto-upload

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and has allowlisted network egress; social-auto-upload handles account data and media files. If they share a workspace, AutoGPT could expose account-linked content or drafts into its own outputs or network calls. The profiles do not show direct secret handling by AutoGPT, so this is a plausible shared-workspace leakage path rather than a confirmed exfiltration route.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or account workspace
IF account data or media files are present in that shared workspace
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points
Keep account files out of AutoGPT's directory
Restrict AutoGPT network destinations to approved endpoints
Rotate or redact account identifiers before shared processing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while social-auto-upload supports multiple instances and uses a one-account-per-file session model. Even though social-auto-upload cannot write files, concurrent access to the same account file or workspace can still cause race conditions and inconsistent uploads. The conflict is plausible in default CLI workflows, but not shown as guaranteed.
conditions: IF AutoGPT launches parallel jobs against the same account file
IF social-auto-upload instances share the same session file or output directory
mitigations: Assign one account file per running instance
Serialize writes to shared directories
Run only one AutoGPT worker per upload workspace
Use OS file locks or a queue for uploads

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate arbitrary instructions or summaries, and social-auto-upload can act on media/account workflows. If social-auto-upload consumes AutoGPT-produced captions, filenames, or task plans without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. The profiles do not document a verification gate, so the safer assumption is a default-path handoff risk.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses AutoGPT-generated text as upload metadata or task input
IF no human review or schema validation occurs before upload
mitigations: Require manual review before posting
Validate captions and filenames against a schema
Compare AutoGPT output to source media before upload
Log and diff proposed actions before execution

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGPT is a general filesystem-and-shell agent, while social-auto-upload touches account data and media tied to social platforms. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if account files or media are processed in a different environment than expected. No specific certifications are documented for either agent, so the compliance risk is inferred and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF account data or media are processed in a jurisdiction or service with different retention rules
IF logs or uploads retain account identifiers beyond the intended policy
mitigations: Minimize retained logs
Store account files in a policy-approved region
Redact identifiers before processing
Document retention and deletion steps for uploads
